result.rationale: Verified from the diff: refreshOAuthTokens' sync branch returns the raw fetch `response` object, while the wired callers expect library-shaped results. GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data; token.access_token` — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so this throws. zoho-bigin/zohocrm call `tokenInfo.data.error` on the returned Response, also undefined. Hubspot expects hubspotClient's parsed token with expiry computed from it. These are all verifiable in the diff and would break whenever CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set.

judged_text: The sync branch returns the raw fetch Response object without calling .json(), while several wired adapters expect library-shaped return values (google-auth-library's res, axios's AxiosResponse, hubspot's parsed HubspotToken). With sync enabled, GoogleCalendarService gets res?.data === undefined and throws TypeError on token.access_token (CalendarService.ts:93-94), zoho-bigin and zohocrm throw TypeError reading tokenInfo.data.error, Hubspot stores undefined tokens with a NaN expiry, and lark's handleLarkError rejects the parent's flat {access_token, expiry} envelope — bookings against these apps fail in sync mode no matter what the operator's endpoint returns.

adjudication.rationale:
Verified in diff: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) and does not call `.json()` or normalize shape (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Multiple call sites continue to treat the return value as a library-specific response/object:
- Google Calendar expects a google-auth-library-like `{ res }` / `res.data` and does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;` which will break because `Response` has no `.data` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`).
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM now wrap `axios` calls with `refreshOAuthTokens` but still access `tokenInfo.data.error` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`; in sync mode this becomes a `Response` without `.data` (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`).
- Hubspot now wraps `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` with `refreshOAuthTokens` but still types/uses it as `HubspotToken`; in sync mode it can be a `Response` instead of the expected token object (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`).
This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and would cause runtime failures in “sync mode”.
